answer: Hardware-anchored identity: each fake costs one distinct ~$40 TPM chip. The node sends a fresh nonce; the agent's quill routine must return a quote signed by a TPM endorsement key whose certificate chains to a vendor anchor. Any key already bound to another address is rejected, so one chip can't back 1,000 fakes, and a VM's hollow emulated TPM has no vendor cert and fails the chain check. Limit: farms can buy chips, but every fake is a separate purchase.
